title: Youth safety funding and ODSP advocacy
subtitle: Building Safer Communities youth grants, crisis response planning, Canada Disability Benefit clawback concerns and a short tracking-list update
overview: The Community and Health Services committee heard an update on the Building Safer Communities project, a federally funded program supporting Indigenous, Black and racialized youth. A youth decision-making team reviewed over fifty applications and awarded nearly $1 million to seventeen organizations for mental health and addiction prevention. The committee received the report for information. Staff said a second grant call has launched and that a youth-focused crisis response model will be co-designed in 2025.

The committee also recommended that the Region call on the Province of Ontario to raise, or at least maintain, ODSP rates once the Canada Disability Benefit begins in 2025 {{vote:m1}}. The motion will be circulated to area municipalities and AMO. The sponsor said residents are worried the province could claw back ODSP when the federal benefit starts, which could add pressure on local supports.
The meeting was brief and ended early. The next meeting is December 3, 2024.

decisions.item: ODSP rates and the Canada Disability Benefit
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that the Region call on Ontario to raise, or at least maintain, ODSP rates once the Canada Disability Benefit starts in 2025, and that the motion be sent to area municipalities and AMO {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Staff said the crisis response model will focus on youth because the grant is youth-specific. They hope it could be used more widely if it works, and it is being designed with police to define when a police presence is not needed.
A councillor asked about school boards. Staff said they have not yet worked with them but see it as a major opportunity.

A councillor raised concern about organizations working in silos. Staff said the Community Safety and Well-being Plan, the Upstream Fund and the Children and Youth Planning Table are meant to build capacity rather than duplicate effort.

A delegate from the Indigenous-led program said trust is the basis of collaboration and called for more Indigenous representation at decision-making tables. A youth delegate urged that the youth decision-making team continue beyond a one-time effort.

On the ODSP motion, the sponsor said it may look beyond the Region's jurisdiction but that a possible provincial clawback would strain local supports. Other councillors voiced support, noting ODSP rates are below the poverty line and that the motion costs nothing.
